plain_rule: A written Arabic word may carry a prefixed particle (wāw, fāʾ, bāʾ, kāf, lām, or the article al-); its contribution is part of the meaning and must be shown, not hidden inside the host word.
trigger_condition: the token begins with a legal proclitic sequence
typical_error_feature: the whole token read as one stem
point_template: Look again at the start of this word: it may begin with a small attached particle.
teach_template: When a word starts with wāw/fāʾ/bāʾ/kāf/lām or al-, that piece is a separate particle with its own meaning; read the host without it, then add the particle's contribution.
bottom_out_template: Split the word into the prefixed particle and the host, and gloss each piece.

curriculum_error_examples.en: A learner sees a word beginning with a sun letter and still pronounces a full lam, treating every al- prefix the same regardless of the letter that follows it.
A learner reads a prefixed particle and its host as one unfamiliar word instead of separating the small attached piece from the host first.

plain_rule: A pronoun attached to the end of a word (a possessive on a noun, an object on a verb) is a separate piece of meaning; a single-letter ending can also be a root letter, so without context it stays a candidate.
trigger_condition: the token ends in a possible enclitic pronoun
expected_feature: the attached pronoun surfaced, or the token kept pending
typical_error_feature: the ending folded into the stem
point_template: Look at the ending of this word: it may be an attached pronoun rather than part of the root.
teach_template: An attached pronoun at the end carries 'his/her/their/you/us'; but a lone single letter could also be a radical, so confirm from context before deciding.
bottom_out_template: Separate the enclitic pronoun from the stem and name its reference.

curriculum_error_examples.en: A learner treats the final letter of a word as part of the root instead of checking whether it is an attached pronoun pointing back to someone or something already mentioned.
A learner assumes an attached pronoun always matches the word it is written on, rather than the person or thing it actually refers to.

plain_rule: Without short vowels, the same letters can be more than one word; keep every reading as a candidate and do not pick one until evidence appears.
trigger_condition: an unvoweled token with more than one reading
expected_feature: the competing readings kept and ranked
point_template: These letters can be read more than one way; notice that the short vowels are missing.
teach_template: Unvoweled Arabic underdetermines the word: the same letters may be a noun or a verb. Keep the readings side by side and let context or a source decide.
bottom_out_template: List the competing readings with their ranking; do not assert one.

curriculum_error_examples.en: A learner picks the more familiar reading of an unvoweled word and drops the other possible reading, instead of keeping both until something in the sentence decides.
A learner assumes every letter in an unvoweled word is a root letter without checking whether one of them actually belongs to the pattern instead.

plain_rule: Some particles (mā, wāw, lā, in, ...) have several functions; the function is decided by context, not by the surface form alone.
trigger_condition: the token is or contains a multi-function particle
expected_feature: the particle's function decided from context
point_template: This little word has several possible jobs here; look at what surrounds it.
teach_template: A particle like mā or wāw can be negation, a relative, a question, coordination, and more; identify the function from the clause, then gloss it accordingly.
bottom_out_template: Name the particle's function in this clause and its effect.

curriculum_error_examples.en: A learner assigns one fixed English meaning to a small particle without checking whether the surrounding words point to a different job for it here.
A learner treats a multi-function particle as only ever a connector, missing that the same shape can mark a wish, a question, or an exception depending on the sentence.

plain_rule: A prefixed preposition (bāʾ, lām, kāf) forms a jar-majrūr with the following word; the relation must be shown, not the host alone.
point_template: There is a prefixed preposition here; it links to the word it governs.
teach_template: A prefixed preposition makes the following noun genitive (majrūr); read them as a phrase and show the relation.
bottom_out_template: Name the preposition and the genitive noun it governs.

arabic_grammar_name: case / mood from context (al-iʿrāb bi-ḥasab al-siyāq)
plain_rule: The case or mood ending depends on the governing element; when the ending is not visible, the reading stays a candidate until context confirms it.
trigger_condition: case/mood is not decidable from the surface
typical_error_feature: a case asserted with no visible ending
point_template: Look at the ending here and at the word that governs it before deciding the case or mood.
teach_template: A case or mood ending is assigned by a governing element; name that governor and the case it requires, and if it is not visible, keep the reading pending.
bottom_out_template: State the governor and the case/mood it assigns.

curriculum_error_examples.en: A learner assigns a case ending from a general rule without checking whether the clause's polarity or structure changes which rule actually applies here.
A learner marks a noun by habit without checking whether the sentence's negation blocks that marking in this position.

arabic_grammar_name: the governing element (al-ʿāmil) justifies the iʿrāb
plain_rule: A correct ending is not enough: the governing element must justify it. A right ending with an absent or wrong governor is unsafe reasoning and goes to review.
trigger_condition: a case is asserted without a justified governor
expected_feature: the case justified by a named governor
typical_error_feature: right answer, wrong or absent reason
point_template: Name the element that governs this word before you justify its ending.
teach_template: The ending must be justified by the ʿāmil (the governing element); naming the right case with the wrong or no governor is unsafe and is routed to review, not accepted.
bottom_out_template: Identify the governor, then justify the assigned case/mood from it.

curriculum_error_examples.en: A learner names a correct case ending but cannot say which word or particle actually requires it, treating the right answer as its own justification.
A learner assumes the nearest word is always the one assigning the case, without checking whether an earlier element in the clause is the real governor.

plain_rule: An orthographic variant (hamza seat, alif form, tāʾ marbūṭa, alif maqṣūra) is normalized for matching only; the original spelling is preserved and may itself be significant.
typical_error_feature: the variant treated as an error
point_template: Notice the spelling of this letter; it is a variant that is normalized only for matching.
teach_template: Hamza seats and alif/tāʾ forms vary in writing; the original spelling is kept, and only a match key is normalized.
bottom_out_template: Show the original spelling and the normalized match key side by side.

arabic_grammar_name: hidden proclitic in a composed token (sābiq multaṣiq lam yuḥtasab)
plain_rule: When a written token carries a prefixed particle (wāw, fāʾ, bāʾ, lām, kāf, or al-), the gloss must account for that prefix; a hover that shows only the host word has dropped a real piece of the meaning.
trigger_condition: a source-addressed hover shows only the host of a token that begins with a proclitic
expected_feature: the proclitic and the host each accounted for in the hover
typical_error_feature: the whole token glossed as the bare host
point_template: Look at the start of this word: a small attached particle is part of it, and the hover has left it out.
teach_template: A prefixed wāw/fāʾ/bāʾ/lām/kāf or al- is a separate piece with its own meaning; the hover must show the host and add the prefix's contribution, not the host alone.
bottom_out_template: Split the token into the prefixed particle and the host, and give each piece its own contribution.

curriculum_error_examples.en: A hover shows only the host word and drops a prefixed particle that changes whether the token is a question word or a preposition.

arabic_grammar_name: dropped attached pronoun (ḍamīr muttaṣil saqaṭa mina l-hover)
plain_rule: An attached pronoun at the end of a token (an object on a verb, a possessive on a noun) is part of the meaning; a gloss that drops it under-reports the token.
trigger_condition: a source-addressed hover omits a token's attached pronoun
expected_feature: the attached pronoun surfaced with its reference
typical_error_feature: the ending folded into the stem and lost
point_template: Look at the ending of this word: an attached pronoun is there, and the hover has not accounted for it.
teach_template: An attached pronoun carries 'his/her/their/you/us'; the hover must keep it and name what it refers to, not fold it into the stem.
bottom_out_template: Separate the attached pronoun from the stem and name its reference.

curriculum_error_examples.en: A learner reads a verb's final letter as decoration and misses that it is an object pronoun, so the object of the action disappears from the reading.
A learner keeps a possessive pronoun on a word after the following noun that licensed it has been dropped.

plain_rule: A finite passive verb must keep its passive contribution in the gloss; reading it as active changes who does and who receives the action.
trigger_condition: a hover glosses a passive verb as active or as a bare dictionary form
expected_feature: the passive voice preserved in the gloss (e.g. 'was created', not 'created' or 'to create')
typical_error_feature: an active or infinitive gloss on a passive verb
point_template: Check the voice of this verb before glossing: it is passive, and an active reading changes the meaning.
teach_template: A passive verb reports that the action was done to its subject; keep that in the gloss ('was created', 'is said'), not an active or dictionary form.
bottom_out_template: State the verb's voice, then give a passive gloss that matches it.

arabic_grammar_name: hidden dual/plural ending (ʿalāmat tathniya aw jamʿ maṭwiyya)
plain_rule: A visible dual or plural ending carries the number; a hover that shows only a singular host, or carries the number only in English, has hidden the ending that teaches it.
trigger_condition: a hover hides a token's visible dual or plural ending
expected_feature: the dual/plural ending shown as part of the breakdown
typical_error_feature: a plain singular host span with the number carried only in English
point_template: Look at the ending of this word: it marks a dual or plural, and the hover has not shown it.
teach_template: The dual ending and the plural endings carry the number; the breakdown must show the ending, not only an English 'two' or a plain host.
bottom_out_template: Point to the dual or plural ending and name the number it marks.

curriculum_error_examples.en: A learner reports a noun's number only from the English translation and does not point to the ending that actually marks it as two or many.
A learner keeps a plural ending on a form after its role in the sentence changes, without checking whether that ending is still licensed there.

plain_rule: A derived noun (an active or passive participle and its kin) is not the verb; its derivative shape must be visible, and it is never glossed as a verb.
trigger_condition: a hover hides a token's derivative prefix/pattern or glosses a derivative as a verb
expected_feature: the derivative shape shown and glossed as a noun/adjective, not a verb
typical_error_feature: a verb gloss on a participle, or the derivative prefix hidden in one span
point_template: This word is a derived noun, not the verb; look for its prefix and pattern before glossing.
teach_template: A participle or other derived noun carries a shape (often a mīm prefix and a fixed pattern); show that shape and gloss it as the doer/done-to or a quality, never as the verb.
bottom_out_template: Name the derivative type and give a noun/adjective gloss, showing the prefix or pattern.

curriculum_error_examples.en: A learner glosses a derived noun with the same English verb it comes from, instead of describing the person or thing that does or receives the action.
A learner assumes every derived noun takes one fixed vowel pattern without first checking which class of verb it was built from.

plain_rule: A finite verb or a derived noun must not be glossed with the dictionary infinitive ('to ...'); the entry headword is a lookup form, not the token's contribution.
trigger_condition: a hover glosses an inflected token with the entry infinitive
expected_feature: a gloss that matches the token's actual form, not the entry 'to ...'
typical_error_feature: the dictionary 'to ...' pasted onto a finite or derived form
point_template: This is the entry's lookup form, not what the word says here; match the gloss to the actual form.
teach_template: The dictionary infinitive ('to write') is the lookup headword; the token in context is finite or derived, so gloss what it actually contributes, not the headword.
bottom_out_template: Give the gloss for the token's real form, and set the entry infinitive aside as lookup-only.

curriculum_error_examples.en: A learner copies the dictionary's 'to ...' gloss onto a verb that is actually conjugated in the text, instead of glossing the form that is actually there.
A learner invents one all-purpose noun for 'the act of doing X' without checking whether that particular verb actually has a noun in that shape.

arabic_grammar_name: phrase gloss on a single token (tarjamat al-ʿibāra makāna al-kalima)
plain_rule: One token's hover must show that token's own contribution; a whole-phrase English translation borrowed from neighbouring words over-claims what the single token means.
trigger_condition: a token's hover carries a multi-word phrase translation that belongs to the surrounding words
expected_feature: the token's own contribution separated from the phrase context
typical_error_feature: a phrase gloss pinned to one token
point_template: This hover gives the whole phrase; ask what this single word contributes on its own.
teach_template: A neighbouring word may supply the subject, object, or relation; record that separately. The token's own hover shows only its piece, not the whole English phrase.
bottom_out_template: Give the token's own contribution, and name which neighbouring word supplies the rest of the phrase.

arabic_grammar_name: token outside the source-address graph (kharija ʿan al-ʿunwana al-maṣdariyya)
plain_rule: A hover claim needs a resolvable source address in the graph; a token that is not a graph node stays out of scope and cannot be certified from the surface alone.
trigger_condition: a claim targets a token with no source-address edge in the graph
expected_feature: the missing edge named and the claim held out of scope
typical_error_feature: a hover certified for a token that has no addressable home
point_template: Check that this token has a real source address before trusting the hover; here the address does not resolve.
teach_template: The engine certifies a hover against a source-addressed occurrence; when the token is not a node in the graph, name the missing edge and keep it out of scope rather than certifying from the surface.
bottom_out_template: Name the exact missing source-address edge and route the token to the validator lane.

arabic_grammar_name: display-local index mistaken for the canonical address (fahras maḥallī laysa al-ʿunwān al-qiyāsī)
plain_rule: A card-local word index that merely looks like sūrah:āyah:word is not the canonical address; a hover may be keyed only once the crosswalk to the canonical address exists.
trigger_condition: a hover is keyed to a display-local index with no crosswalk to the canonical address
expected_feature: the canonical crosswalk present before the hover is keyed
typical_error_feature: an orphan hover appended at a card-local index treated as canonical
point_template: Check whether this location is the canonical address or only a card-local index before keying the hover.
teach_template: Some cards number words with a card-local index that only looks canonical; before a hover is keyed, confirm the crosswalk to the real sūrah:āyah:word, or keep the row pending with the missing anchor.
bottom_out_template: Produce the crosswalk to the canonical address, or hold the row pending with the exact missing anchor.

arabic_grammar_name: public-boundary source leak (kharq ḥudūd al-naẓāfa al-ʿāmma)
plain_rule: A learner-facing gloss must be authored, never copied external source, brand, or provenance text; a boundary violation never ships.
trigger_condition: a hover or hint text carries copied external source/brand/provenance wording
typical_error_feature: external source wording pasted into the public gloss
point_template: This text carries wording that belongs to an internal source; the public gloss must be authored, not copied.
teach_template: Public learner text is authored in-house; source names, brands, and provenance labels route review internally but never become the public gloss. Rewrite the piece in your own words.
bottom_out_template: Replace the copied wording with an authored, source-clean gloss; a boundary violation never ships.
